tasks.short: Write and publish product descriptions from supplier information and verified product facts.

steps.what: Gather supplier specifications, existing descriptions and brand guidance.
Check source claims against product records and resolve missing attributes.

loop.input: Supplier specifications and product records for one product.
loop.output: Proposed attributes with source references, conflicts and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate field types and units; compare identifiers; require review of unsupported or conflicting claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per product; unresolved fields return to the online merchant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields use direct mapping. Mixed prose and inconsistent specification layouts need extraction.

steps.what: Draft product descriptions using verified facts and brand guidance.
Approve accuracy, tone and customer-facing claims.
Enter approved descriptions into product listings and publish.

tasks.design: An intake integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles sources from {DOCS} and {ERP}; a bounded extraction loop proposes facts for review. Configure description drafting in the {ECOMMERCE} from approved facts and guidance, using templates for standard specification sections. A {WORKFLOW} approval releases the exact approved copy through the {ECOMMERCE}, with version checks and publication logs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier facts arrived in inconsistent documents. Copy tools and product records were poorly connected, so merchants gathered and re-entered information.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing description generators can be configured. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building source intake, validation and publishing connections.
tasks.still_hard: Unsupported claims, ambiguous specifications, specialist terminology and market-specific wording still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: The merchant decides which benefits matter to customers and whether a claim fairly represents the product.

ambition.what: Second-language product pages for one additional EU market.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from drafting and copying toward checking claims and improving weak listings. Additional market launches still require commercial approval; publication rights stay within the existing delegation.

reach.task: Review a reusable product style guide and terminology list.
reach.learn: Learn editorial consistency, claim qualification and how to write useful review criteria.

reach.task: Validate terminology for the additional market.
reach.learn: Learn locale-specific phrasing, units and when literal translation misleads.

evidence.claim: An existing commerce assistant can draft product descriptions; this supports trying configuration first.
Source assembly, field validation and approved-copy publishing can use deterministic integrations.

assumptions: The company has product identifiers shared across sources and listings.
A configured drafting feature can accept approved facts; otherwise a bounded drafting loop is needed.
Publication uses only the approved version; changed facts or copy trigger renewed approval.
Build ranges cover one storefront and one initial language.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the actual deployment. National rules govern any employee consultation.
unknowns: Which drafting, approval and publishing capabilities the current {ECOMMERCE} provides.
Whether supplier documents may be processed by the proposed model service.
Who approves specialist claims and additional languages.
Which employee consultation and access approvals apply.
research_questions: Can configured drafting preserve every approved attribute without adding unsupported benefits?
Which source layouts produce extraction errors on a representative product sample?
new_work: Review extracted conflicts and missing attributes.
Check generated claims and maintain terminology.
Maintain source mappings and channel requirements.
Handle failed publications and version conflicts.

tasks.short: Plan, photograph or film products, then edit and approve accurate merchandising images.

steps.what: Prepare the shot list from product facts and campaign requirements.
Arrange product samples, lighting, backgrounds and props.
Capture product photographs or video with cameras.
Select and edit captures in {OTHER} photo and video editing software.
Approve visual quality and faithful representation of the product.
Export approved masters and record product identifiers in the media library.

tasks.design: A template generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} creates draft shot lists from approved product facts and stores them in {DOCS}. Configure batch presets in {OTHER} photo and video editing software while the merchant directs capture, selects images and approves product fidelity. An integration stores approved masters, identifiers and approval records in {DOCS} for the upload workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical staging and visual judgement dominate the task. Repetitive editing and export work often lacked consistent presets and identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing batch-editing features and small deterministic utilities can reduce preparation and file handling. No breakthrough in physical capture is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Reflective surfaces, colour accuracy, texture, scale and convincing demonstrations require skilled capture and review.
tasks.human_edge: The merchant notices which angle or demonstration makes the real product understandable and desirable.

ambition.what: Product fit demonstrations for one high-return product category.

tasks.altitude: The merchant spends less time preparing files and more time directing shoots and testing demonstrations. Creative decisions remain human; any new service needs the existing budget approval.

reach.task: Develop consistent lighting, cropping and visual presentation standards.
reach.learn: Learn colour management, composition and faithful retouching.

reach.task: Design product galleries that explain scale and fit.
reach.learn: Learn mobile image sequencing, accessibility and media performance.

evidence.claim: Shot-list templates, batch editing presets and file export can reduce repetitive media preparation.
Physical capture and product-fidelity review remain substantial human work.

assumptions: The merchant performs routine product photography; specialists handle some complex shoots.
Approved masters are preserved separately from edited derivatives.
The first release uses established editing presets and does not generate replacement product appearances.
Build ranges cover one media library and one editing environment.
GDPR applies if identifiable people appear. EU AI Act requirements apply to any later AI features; national rules govern relevant employee consultation.
unknowns: Which batch features and export interfaces the {OTHER} editing software supports.
How product samples, image rights and approval records are managed.
Whether staff or external models appear in product media.
Which national consultation requirements apply to changed working practices.
research_questions: Which preset operations preserve colour and material detail across representative products?
Which demonstration format best explains fit without increasing page load excessively?
new_work: Maintain shot-list templates and editing presets.
Inspect batch results for colour or cropping errors.
Maintain media identifiers and approval records.
Plan and evaluate the proposed product demonstrations.

tasks.short: Prepare approved product media, upload it to sales channels and check the live listings.

steps.what: Find approved media and match files to products and channels.
Resize, encode and rename media using {OTHER} media processing software.
Upload media, set gallery order and save listing changes.
Preview the gallery and approve its product association and sequence.
Publish approved media and check the live listing.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads approved packages from {DOCS}, validates product identifiers and produces an upload manifest. Configured media presets create channel derivatives, and connectors stage them in the {ECOMMERCE} for gallery approval. A {WORKFLOW} publishes the approved version, checks media availability and sends failures through {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approval records, file names and product identifiers were disconnected. Different channel requirements encouraged repeated screen work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing media presets handle conversion. AI-assisted coding makes channel adapters, manifests and retry controls cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Some channels lack useful interfaces. Crops, gallery meaning and inconsistent product identifiers still create exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: The merchant spots misleading image sequences and chooses which views best answer customer questions.
tasks.altitude: Upload sessions become short gallery reviews and exception handling. Nothing changes in commercial decision rights.

reach.task: Check product gallery behaviour on mobile and with assistive technology.
reach.learn: Learn responsive media, keyboard navigation and accessible gallery descriptions.

evidence.claim: File conversion, identifier matching and media upload are predominantly deterministic operations.
Channel variation and visual gallery approval can limit fully unattended publication.

assumptions: Media creation and master approval are covered by the preceding task.
Channel-native bulk upload is configured first where it satisfies the requirements.
Human approval applies to the staged gallery; the publishing job cannot change its content or sequence.
Build ranges cover one storefront and one additional sales channel.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed where relevant. National consultation rules are checked if the rollout introduces employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which channels support staging, bulk media upload and publication interfaces.
Whether product identifiers are reliable across channels.
How approval and rollback work in the current {ECOMMERCE}.
Which access permissions and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can each channel preserve gallery order and avoid duplicate uploads after retries?
Which transformations need visual review rather than file-level validation?
new_work: Resolve identifier mismatches and failed uploads.
Maintain channel format rules and connector credentials.
Monitor publication checks and remove duplicate derivatives.

tasks.short: Combine sales and expense records, reconcile differences and calculate trading totals.

steps.what: Export orders, discounts, cancellations and refunds from the {ECOMMERCE}.
Retrieve booked revenue, fees and expenses from the {ERP}.
Match exports and flag missing entries or inconsistent totals.
Calculate sales, revenue and expense totals using workbook formulas.
Ask the finance team to explain missing costs and accounting differences.
Review totals and explanations, then release the trading report.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled exports from the {ECOMMERCE} and {ERP}; a deterministic job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles identifiers, periods and control totals. Configure agreed calculations in the {BI}, with source dates and unresolved differences visible beside the figures. A small records app in the {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions to the finance team and records the merchant's report approval without posting ledger adjustments.
tasks.previous_blocker: The arithmetic was already supported by software. Different exports, accounting definitions and missing cost entries kept reconciliation in workbooks and email.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled exports and existing reporting features provide the base. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings, controls and exception handling.
tasks.still_hard: Revenue recognition, VAT treatment, currency conversion, late refunds and shared-cost allocation require finance judgement and agreed definitions.
tasks.human_edge: The merchant interprets trading changes and challenges whether the figures reflect the commercial reality.

ambition.what: A daily channel contribution review using agreed attributable costs.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting exports and rebuilding totals toward reviewing trading changes and resolving material differences. More frequent information supports recommendations; pricing and spending rights remain under existing delegations.

reach.task: Use channel contribution evidence to recommend campaign budget changes.
reach.learn: Learn cost attribution, uncertainty and the difference between revenue growth and profitable growth.

reach.role: market research analysts and marketing specialists
reach.task: Investigate whether sales changes reflect demand, seasonality or promotions.
reach.learn: Learn comparison design and how to avoid treating correlation as campaign impact.

evidence.claim: Sales and expense calculations usually need deterministic mappings, formulas and reconciliation controls.
A governed dashboard can replace repeated workbook preparation while leaving accounting exceptions with people.

assumptions: The {ERP} remains the source for booked financial amounts.
Trading reports are management reports; ledger changes and statutory filings are outside this build.
Customer-level personal data is excluded where aggregate records suffice.
Daily contribution is provisional until costs are complete and agreed.
Build ranges cover one ledger and one storefront, with existing reporting infrastructure.
EU GDPR and EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the deployment. National rules govern consultation if monitoring of employees is introduced.
unknowns: Which exports, scheduled reports and interfaces are available.
Whether sales and ledger records share stable matching identifiers.
Which revenue, tax, currency and cost-allocation definitions the finance team approves.
Whether daily attributable cost data is complete enough for contribution reporting.
Which financial access permissions and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can reconciliation handle refunds, partial settlements and period cutoffs without silent double counting?
What freshness and completeness indicators make provisional daily figures useful?
new_work: Maintain account mappings and metric definitions.
Resolve unmatched records with the finance team.
Monitor missing feeds, late costs and reconciliation failures.
Review material changes before releasing reports.

role.altitude: The merchant spends more time on product truth, visual direction and trading decisions, with less copying, uploading and workbook preparation. Automation does not itself grant new budget, pricing or accounting authority.
reach: Work with editors and translators on credible product pages for an additional market.
Work with graphic designers and interface designers on demonstrations and useful product galleries.
Work with marketing managers on channel contribution and campaign recommendations.
skills_to_grow: Product claim verification and editorial review.
Photography direction, colour fidelity and accessible media.
Financial reconciliation, metric definitions and cost attribution.
Exception handling and practical evaluation of automated outputs.
role.ambitious_version: Run a repeatable merchandising improvement service that combines trustworthy localized pages, product fit demonstrations and daily channel contribution reviews, within delegated commercial limits.
